intent_en: To demonstrate that the United States tax system is largely flat rather than progressive when all tax types are combined, challenging the common perception that the wealthy pay a significantly higher share of their income.
previous_intent: To demonstrate that when all tax types are combined, the U.S. tax system is largely flat rather than progressive, revealing that the wealthiest individuals pay a lower overall tax burden than lower-income groups.
narration_support: That America's tax system as a whole isn't very progressive. Instead, it's mostly flat.
chart_support: Stacked bar chart displaying the total tax burden (sum of income, payroll, consumption, estate, and corporate/property taxes) as a percentage of income across income groups from poorest to richest, showing that total tax rates are relatively similar (flat) across the spectrum and lower for the highest earners than for the peak earners.
evidence_note: The narration explicitly claims the system is 'mostly flat' and the richest pay less than the poorest. The chart supports this by showing total bar heights (total tax %) are roughly comparable for the poorest (~25% visual estimate) and richest (~22% visual estimate) groups, with the rightmost bar being lower than the leftmost.
